summary: Tucked into just 4.4 square miles between the tidal marshlands of San Francisco Bay and the steep, oak-studded flanks of Mount Tamalpais, Corte Madera occupies a geographic slot so compressed that you can walk from wetland boardwalks to ridgeline fire roads in under an hour. Highway 101 bisects the town almost evenly, creating a real structural divide between the flatter eastern neighborhoods near the bay and the hillside homes climbing west toward Ring Mountain, a protected open space preserve harboring rare wildflowers found almost nowhere else on Earth. The Town Center and The Village at Corte Madera—two sizable retail clusters flanking the freeway—give this tiny municipality an outsized commercial footprint, pulling shoppers from across Marin County, which means weekend traffic can feel incongruent with the population of under 10,000. With a median home price around $1.7 million against a median household income near $221,000, the price-to-income ratio lands at roughly 7.7×—steep, but notably less punishing than some neighboring Marin towns. Average daily highs hover around 66°F year-round under nine hours of sunshine, yielding a mild, fog-modulated climate where summer afternoons rarely feel hot. Corte Madera functions largely as a bedroom community for San Francisco, roughly a 25-minute drive south without traffic, though Golden Gate Transit buses and ferry connections from nearby Larkspur Landing offer alternatives. The defining tension here is scale versus gravity: a town small enough to feel cohesive, yet bisected by a freeway and anchored by regional retail centers that make it punch well above its weight in commerce while remaining fundamentally residential.
